theme: Core Data in practice: background work, conflicts and live lists

terms.definition: A second context that does slow work on a background queue, so the screen stays smooth.
terms.example: Import the data in a background context.

terms.definition: A rule that decides which version wins when two contexts change the same object.
terms.example: Set a merge policy so the newest change wins.
terms.code:
import CoreData
let ctx = NSManagedObjectContext(.mainQueue)
ctx.mergePolicy = NSOverwriteMergePolicy
print(ctx.mergePolicy is NSMergePolicy)

terms.definition: A helper that watches a fetch request and tells a table view when the results change.
terms.example: An NSFetchedResultsController keeps the list in sync.

video.description:
Learn to explain how Core Data does slow work off the main thread and keeps lists up to date: Background Context, Merge Policy & NSFetchedResultsController, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Background Context - A second context that does slow work on a background queue, so the screen stays smooth.
Merge Policy - A rule that decides which version wins when two contexts change the same object.
NSFetchedResultsController - A helper that watches a fetch request and tells a table view when the results change.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Background Context, Merge Policy and NSFetchedResultsController in English?

dialogue.title: The frozen import

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the screen freezes when we import a thousand notes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You import on the main queue. Use a background context instead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A background context does the slow work, so the screen stays smooth.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But now my edit and the import change the same note.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then you need a merge policy. It decides which version wins.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I set `mergePolicy` to `NSOverwriteMergePolicy`. Is that right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It makes the new change win. Pick the merge policy that fits your app.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The list does not show the imported notes, though.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add an NSFetchedResultsController. It watches the fetch request and reports the changes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the table view updates by itself?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The background context saves, and the NSFetchedResultsController tells the list.
Import in a background context, not on the main queue.
